mathematical_summary: For A0=[[C,B],[B^T,D]] with C invertible, Q=C^{-1}B, S=D-B^TC^{-1}B and G=[I;Q^T], every symmetric K satisfies A0+GKG^T=R^T diag(C+K,S)R. Thus arbitrary signed gauge spectrum leaves the Schur remainder exactly invariant. In the scalar case a local exact identity bounds the final physical Schur crossing using only pivot/cross blocks of a non-gauge tail; same-bank tail blocks are free for this certificate.

partner.actual_application: At the exact rank-one self endpoint the partner proves s2(B#)>=g. The Schur-gauge theorem preserves B# through the unbounded signed gauge packet and degrades it only by eps_loc under the residual tail, giving s2(B#_final)>=g-eps_loc.

concrete_target_family.baseline: m=3, C0=diag(2,0,0), B0=[[2,0],[0,2],[2,0]], arbitrary complementary symmetric block

unresolved_implication: From bare s3(A)>=1, prove that some original-coordinate pivot admits a quantitatively nondegenerate Schur-gauge approximation with a surviving paid cross/ridge certificate, or prove that failure of all such approximations forces an already-paid D5/projected-crossing/ridge/pair/grouped-bank/half-Riesz exit.
